g.textArea: Execution policy: explicit final-plan approval for staging/production is proposed; dev approval policy remains a team decision.
Failure rule: failed or changed final plan blocks apply; regenerate and renew authorization. PR updates rerun checks and review.
Target comes from the selected root, inputs and backend/state. Each environment has its own plan; promotion does not reuse a dev plan.

g.textArea: GitHub Actions runner executes commands; the target is the cloud infrastructure selected by the Terraform root.
01D Terraform: branches and promotion
CTO / developers / DevOps | Draft recommendation | Merge reviewed code once; authorize and verify each environment separately.
Blue = proposed process | Gray = explanation or evidence | Yellow = gate, alternative or team decision
Three different choices

rect.data-content:
Branch / commit
Which version of the code is selected.
A branch name alone does not select dev or prod.

Environment target
Configuration folder + inputs + state
and cloud identity select what is changed.

Release / tag
An optional label for a specific version.
It can identify the version tested in dev first.

g.textArea: Recommended per-change flow: main branch with explicit promotion

rect.data-content:
1. Review the PR
Checks and preview plans.
Review code and target impact.

2. Merge to main
Record the exact revision.
Production does not run
just because code merged.

3. Apply to dev
Generate the final dev plan.
Authorize under dev policy.
Actions applies that plan.

4. Verify dev
Check deployed settings.
Run acceptance tests.
Record the evidence.

5. Promote to staging
Select the tested version.
Own plan, approval and apply.
Verify staging requirements.

6. Promote to production
Select the tested version.
Own plan, approval and apply.
Verify production requirements.

Alternative: dev branch, then main branch
This can work if workflows explicitly map each branch to its target.
The branch mapping and each execution gate are team decisions.

Required checks fail: stop promotion
Correct the change, review it again and regenerate affected plans.
A successful apply alone does not establish acceptance.

Promote a configuration version, not a dev plan file
Each environment needs its own plan against its settings and current state. Never apply the dev plan to production.
With separate folders, explicitly update the next target's configuration or tested module version; a tag does not copy edits between folders.

Team decisions: dev auto-apply versus approval; who accepts tests and authorizes promotion; revision/tag/module-version strategy.
GitHub approval support depends on repository visibility and plan. This is per-change promotion, separate from rolling out the automation capability.

g.textArea: Saved evidence: existing TL workflow plans development changes only; it has no apply job. Sources: Nov 3–4 snapshot; Terraform apply/plan and GitHub deployment documentation.
01E Terraform: verify the requirements
Reviewers / QA / DevOps | Draft | Define measurable acceptance criteria before apply, then test the actual environment.
Blue = proposed process | Gray = explanation or evidence | Yellow = gate, alternative or team decision
Examples to agree with the team; choose criteria and tests for each change

rect.data-content: Before apply: planned configuration
After apply: deployed behavior
Database settings

Private access; agreed region, engine,
capacity and backup settings.

Read back the actual settings.
Confirm the application connects.
Network and access

Only required paths and roles.
Review exposure and permission changes.

Required traffic succeeds.
Unauthorized traffic and identities fail.
Recovery readiness

Backup and recovery configuration
matches the agreed recovery targets.

Run an agreed restore or failover test.
Measure recovery time and data loss.
Capacity and availability

Review sizing, redundancy and limits
against the agreed expected load.

Run health and integration tests.
Measure required load/latency targets.

Configuration validity is one layer
terraform validate checks syntax and consistency.
Plan review checks intended changes and replacements.
Neither proves that user journeys or recovery work.

Acceptance controls promotion
Require the relevant tests to pass before moving on.
Record revision, target, plan approval and apply result.
Keep the test evidence with that deployment.

Agree before implementation: criteria, test owners, thresholds, evidence and exception authority.
Separate code review, authorization to apply, and acceptance to promote. Apply the exact authorized target plan; re-plan and authorize if invalidated.

g.textArea: Reference: HashiCorp validate, plan, apply and test documentation. Terraform integration tests may create real resources; select an agreed test scope. Saved Nov 16, 2026.
